step1_analysis.description: This circuit acts as the comparator and spike generator in an Address-Event Representation (AER) integrate-and-fire pixel. It monitors the integration node (N0) and uses positive feedback to generate a sharp output spike (N2) while accelerating the discharge of the integration node when the threshold is crossed.

max_gain_db.description: Maximum small-signal voltage gain during the comparator transition.

sky130_expected.calculation: Intrinsic gain of the XM3/XM1 inverter stage. gm * (ro3 || ro1). For L=0.5um, intrinsic gain is typically 20-40 V/V.
sky130_expected.reasoning: Matches typical single-stage inverter gain in 130nm process.

trip_voltage.description: The input voltage at N0 where the comparator flips and N2 crosses VLABEL/2.

sky130_expected.reasoning: XM3 turns on when its Vgs exceeds the threshold voltage.

t_delay.description: Rise time of the output spike at N2 (10% to 90% of VLABEL).

sky130_expected.calculation: I_D3 ≈ 57uA. dV/dt = I/C = 57uA / 10fF = 5.7 V/ns. Rise time for 0.72V swing is ~0.13 ns.
sky130_expected.reasoning: SKY130 is much faster than the original 0.6um process, leading to sub-nanosecond rise times for small load capacitances.

energy_spike.description: Energy consumed from the threshold bias supply to generate one spike.

sky130_expected.calculation: E = C * V^2 + E_short_circuit. For 10fF load and 0.9V swing, E_cap = 8.1 fJ. Total energy ~10-20 fJ.
sky130_expected.reasoning: Lower supply voltage (0.9V vs 1V) and smaller parasitic capacitances in 130nm reduce the energy per spike compared to the 0.6um paper.

pwr_stat.description: Static power consumption in the reset/integration state before firing.

sky130_expected.calculation: When N0 is high, XM3 is completely off. Power is dominated by subthreshold leakage.
sky130_expected.reasoning: Static power for a single pixel latch is just leakage current.

step3_testbench.description: Testbench to measure the DC transfer characteristics (gain, trip voltage) and transient spike generation (delay, energy) of the AER pixel latch.
step3_testbench.spice:
* Testbench for Biomorphic Digital Image Sensor Latch
.lib "${SKY130_PDK}" tt

.param W_xm1=5u L_xm1=0.5u
.param W_xm2=5u L_xm2=0.5u
.param W_xm3=5u L_xm3=0.5u
.param W_xm4=5u L_xm4=0.5u

* DUT
XM1 N2 N0 N1 GND sky130_fd_pr__nfet_01v8 l={L_xm1} w={W_xm1}
XM2 N1 N1 GND GND sky130_fd_pr__nfet_01v8 l={L_xm2} w={W_xm2}
XM3 N2 N0 LABEL_NET_0 VDD sky130_fd_pr__pfet_01v8 l={L_xm3} w={W_xm3}
XM4 N0 N1 GND GND sky130_fd_pr__nfet_01v8 l={L_xm4} w={W_xm4}

* Supplies
VVDD VDD 0 1.8
VLABEL LABEL_NET_0 0 0.9

* Input Drive for DC Sweep (Disconnected during Tran)
VN0_src N0_src 0 1.8
.model sw_ideal sw vt=0.5 vh=0.1 ron=1 roff=1e12
S1 N0_src N0 sw_ctrl 0 sw_ideal
Vctrl sw_ctrl 0 dc 1 pwl(0 1 1n 1 2n 0)

* Transient Integration Components (Photodiode emulation)
CN0 N0 0 50f
IN0 N0 0 dc 100n
CN2 N2 0 10f

.control
* 1. DC Analysis
dc VN0_src 0.9 0 -0.001
let gain_mag = abs(deriv(v(N2)))
let gain_db = 20 * log10(gain_mag + 1e-15)
meas dc max_gain_db max gain_db
meas dc trip_voltage find v(N0) when v(N2)=0.45

* 2. Transient Analysis
tran 1n 2u
meas tran t_rise_start trig v(N2) val=0.09 rise=1
meas tran t_rise_end trig v(N2) val=0.81 rise=1
let t_delay = t_rise_end - t_rise_start
print t_delay

let pwr_label = -i(VLABEL) * 0.9
meas tran energy_spike integ pwr_label

let pwr_vdd = -i(VVDD) * 1.8
meas tran energy_vdd integ pwr_vdd

meas tran pwr_stat find pwr_label at=0.5n

quit
.endc
.end
